claims.text: Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict the melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict the enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict the entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict volume changes at melting for high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed machine-learning-potential approach is computationally efficient.
Atomic arrangement and bonding are the structural mediators connecting the applied potentials to thermodynamic predictions.
Ab initio molecular dynamics and density-functional-theory calculations constitute the proposed mechanism underlying the predictions.
The mean absolute error in predicted melting temperature will be less than 50 K relative to experimental values.
The mean absolute error in predicted enthalpy of fusion will be less than 10% relative to experimental values.
The mean absolute error in predicted entropy of fusion will be less than 10% relative to experimental values.
The approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing up to 10 principal elements.
Transferability of the machine-learning potentials to previously unseen high-entropy alloys is uncertain.
The accuracy of the ab initio training data is uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if melting-temperature mean absolute error exceeds 100 K or fusion-enthalpy or fusion-entropy mean absolute error exceeds 20%.
